terms.p: The set of points in your code over which a reference has to stay valid; a lifetime name like 'a is a name for one of these, not a length of time.
The rule that a reference valid for a long region may be used wherever one valid for a shorter region is wanted.
A position in a type where no other lifetime may be swapped in, in either direction, because the value can be both read and written through it.

terms.x: the lifetimes rustc writes for you
terms.p: The compiler filling in lifetime names in a function signature using three fixed rules, so that most signatures need no annotation at all.
